questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Canada because of the amazing nature which I had plenty of opportunities to explore. I also wanted to go on exchange to a country where I would be able to speak with the locals. I lived with two local canadians, so I also got to do that

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UBC had a lot of infomations and where also very easy to get in contact with

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I visited the international office and got help there to finalize my course choices.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through Facebook Marketplace. I sent 5 applications before finding the right place. It was a bit more expensive than student housing, but nothing compared to the other places I looked at. There is a housing crisis in Vancouver, so it can be difficult to find something within a student's budget.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that I moved in somewhere that actually felt like a home.Student housing is completely empty when you move in, so you have to buy everything like pots and pans and so on. I'm really glad that I didn't have to do that. UBC is almost like its own little city, so if you want to get the feeling of living in Vancouver, I would recommend finding a place in Kitsilano or Mount Pleasant. However, you will then spend more time in public transportation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You answer a survey for UBC where you apply to 10 different courses in prioritised order. You get the answers to the survey 2 months later. However, I got into my number 3,4,9,10, which are the only courses not at the sciences department. When I returned to UBC, asking to get into some of my science courses, they were all full. I tried to find some relevant courses, but I ended up needing to visit the international office to finalize my choices. They were very helpful at the office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office both had an email and office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. Only two out of four courses where the ones I wanted. It is very diffircult to get into courses in computer science or statistics

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that courses at the science departments are much more restrictive and can be very difficult to get into if you are not in the exact same program. That might cause problems if you are in a more interdisciplinary program at KU

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 400 course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Some lectures and some discussion gruops. We were only 15 students in one of the courses I had, so it was more student led

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of the environment
Critical disability studies 
Advanced Econometrics
Globalization and Social Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of the environment and if possible a course with professor Puar which where the one who had the critical disability course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Fresh produce are very expensive in Canada, more than I had expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is covered in your fees to UBC. Not that expensive to rent cars

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many clubs at UBC. I was part of the ski and board club, surf club and crafts club. All clubs had parties and trips throughout the term

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ski and board club and surf club. Both clubs had great parties and deals with companies so you can get a good deal on equipment

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking. It is wo easy to get to great hiking trails if you rent a car. Go to vancouver island, banff and jasper

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. canadians are very friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live off campus. Be a club member

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendlyness, It is very easy to get in contact with candians

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to visit canada, it is very usefull to have a drivers license, but the nature in Canada is beautiful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time when choosing courses. It can be diffircult to get into other courses later on, so be proactive

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balacing the workload with all the things you want to do outside of Uni

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
